Fold one release of a source into the ledger

Source: R/md-ledger.R
md_apply_release.Rd

Takes a parsed release - a table or view with the standard frame columns (see the md_parse_*() functions) - and applies the update rule for the source's kind (md_source_kinds()), in one transaction:

Usage

md_apply_release(
  con,
  frame,
  source,
  version,
  part = NA,
  vintage = version,
  file_md5 = NA
)

Arguments

con

A DuckDB connection holding the ledger.

frame

A table or view in con with the standard frame columns.

source

A source from md_sources().

version

The pinned version.

part

The partition (tax year), or NA.

vintage

What the release describes, as a sortable string ("2026-07"). Defaults to version. Orders snapshot releases.

file_md5

The md5 of the file read. If a release with this id was already applied from a file with the same md5, nothing is done.

Value

A one-row data frame, invisibly: status (applied, unchanged or already_applied), n_rows, n_new, n_kept, n_retracted.

Details

series, mentions, cache, seed

Diff against the ledger rows of this source and partition: new rows are inserted, rows already present have last_release moved to this release, and rows this release no longer carries get retracted_in. A retracted row that comes back is un-retracted. A new partition is all inserts.

snapshot

Compare against the spells left open by the source's previous release: an unchanged value extends its spell, a new or changed value opens one, and a value that is missing is left closed. Releases must arrive in vintage order; an older one is refused, because the fix for a missed release is a replay, not a back-fill.

Applying the same release twice changes nothing. For a snapshot, the second application is reported as already applied; for the other kinds the diff simply finds nothing to do.
